text:
Jordan: Heads up — we started seeing a spike of 5xxs (mostly 503) from h2 clients in US-W region around ~12:05 UTC. Affected tenants are small but constant. Sample request IDs: req=aa12, req=aa13, req=aa17. Error pattern looks like `RST_STREAM` / window update stalls. Anyone on call?

infra-bot: Alert: high_5xx_rate detected on edge-proxy-usw2 (h2) — 12:06 UTC — rate 18/min (baseline 0.8/min).

Maria: On it. Initial look at proxy logs shows a lot of HTTP2 WINDOW_UPDATE backlog and repeated stream resets. Could be client-side or our ingress queueing. I'm pulling tcpdump for one client IP to check RSTs.

Lee: I saw similar earlier in eu region a month ago when a change to default HPACK table growth caused head-of-line stalls. Can you grep for `GOAWAY` and `FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR` in the proxy logs?

Jordan: Grepping now. Found some `GOAWAY` with code PROTOCOL_ERROR and a handful of `RST_STREAM: REFUSED_STREAM`. Also noticing a surge in in-flight conn count for that pool.

Sophie: Customer impact — two paying customers filed support tickets about streaming timeouts and retries doubling their token counts. They're asking if we will credit any overage. Tagging billing once we have root cause. :worried_face:

Maria: Repro attempt: curl against edge with `--http2` hits 503 if I open multiple parallel streams (~40) then close quickly. Minimal reproducer below: 
```
curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream &
# run ~40 in a loop
```
This smells like h2 window/backpressure interplay + our ingress qdisc.

Lee: Possible mitigation — throttle concurrent h2 streams per-conn at the proxy level and add short 50ms jitter on accept path to avoid bursts. We did a fast rollback once for a similar pattern. Can we enable a temporary soft-limit config and observe?

Maria: Pushed a config to decrease max_concurrent_streams from 100 to 16 on the problematic pool (will only affect new conns). Also increased `http2_write_window` timeout. Rolling through canaries in 2 mins.

Jordan: Noted. Communicated to customer that we're investigating and throttling ingress to reduce error rate. Sophie: can you send a brief customer update saying we see h2 stream contention and are applying a temporary throttling patch?

Sophie: Sent. Message: "We're investigating intermittent 503s caused by HTTP/2 stream contention on our US-W edge and have applied temporary throttling while we fix the root cause. We'll follow up with credits if you saw double retries." Customer replied: "Thanks — please prioritize, streaming jobs are blocking our pipelines."

infra-bot: Config rollout to edge-proxy-usw2 started — canary 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%. Status: 25% at 12:15 UTC.

Lee: Early telemetry post-rollout shows 503 rate dropping ~70% on canaries. Keep an eye on connection churn and p95 latency for small clients.

Maria: Follow-ups: 1) collect pcap and h2 frame traces for a few req ids (I'll attach to ticket), 2) schedule a postmortem for next weekday to pin root cause (ingress qdisc vs h2 implementation), 3) consider SDK guidance to backoff and limit parallel streams.

Jordan: Also flagging potential billing hit — customers with streaming SDKs that aggressively retry may have been double-invoiced. Sophie, please open a billing ticket to review those tenant IDs once we have exact retry counts.

Sophie: Will do. Created billing ticket BT-3459 and linked support tickets.

Maria: Next steps: keep canary active, monitor for 30m, collect traces, and if stable, we can push globally. If errors persist, we'll rollback.

Lee: If stable in 30m, let's also run a short load test to validate with synthetic h2 clients hitting 60 parallel streams to ensure we didn't overfit the config.

Jordan: Thanks team. I'll update the original support threads and set a reminder for the postmortem. :thumbsup:
